themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints in parks spiked to 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. a baseline of 0.1 per week, a 3100% increase (z-score: 11.72), suggesting either a new event series, organized gatherings, or enforcement gap in what should be a recreational amenity.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3100% spike, z-score: 11.72)
Aligns with CB budget priority to 'improve access to a park or amenity'—suggesting parks may be underutilized or poorly managed
High statistical severity (z-score 11.72) indicates this is not random variation
reporting_angles: What event or activity triggered the park noise spike this week? Interview Parks Dept and nearby residents.
Are parks in East New York/Cypress Hills equipped with adequate programming or enforcement to manage weekend/evening use?

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 36 THIS WEEK vs. an 8-week average of 8.6 per week, a 317% increase (z-score: 6.12), signaling either construction activity, late-night commerce, or vehicle-related disturbances not previously flagged.
evidence: 36 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 8.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (317% spike, z-score: 6.12)
Occurs in parallel with spike in mobile food vendor complaints (3 complaints 2 weeks ago, +2300%), suggesting street commerce activity may be driver
High statistical confidence (z-score 6.12) rules out statistical noise
reporting_angles: Are mobile food vendors, construction crews, or nightlife venues operating outside permitted hours or without permits?
Canvass residential blocks with highest complaint density to document specific noise sources and times.

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints hit 36 TWO WEEKS AGO vs. a baseline of 4.5 per week, a 700% surge (z-score: 7.09), indicating either coordinated vandalism, gang activity, or a temporary spike that may have subsided—needs current verification.
evidence: 36 graffiti complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 4.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike, z-score: 7.09)
Timing unknown for current status—may have continued or subsided; requires on-the-ground verification
High statistical anomaly (z-score 7.09) suggests this was not routine variation
reporting_angles: Document current graffiti prevalence on major corridors (Jamaica Ave, Atlantic Ave, etc.); has cleanup occurred?
Interview NYPD gang units and Parks enforcement: was this tagged outbreak or ongoing vandalism?

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Neglect
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints spiked to 22 LAST WEEK vs. a baseline of 2.9 per week, a 665% increase (z-score: 5.8), indicating residents perceive sanitation service degradation—possibly related to seasonal street maintenance gaps or staffing shortfalls.
evidence: 22 street sweeping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (665% spike, z-score: 5.8)
Does not yet show if spike continued THIS WEEK; need trend confirmation
High statistical anomaly suggests genuine service gap, not random complaint variation
reporting_angles: Obtain Sanitation Dept schedule data: are East New York/Cypress Hills receiving proportional sweeping coverage vs. other Brooklyn CDs?
Geospatial analysis: which blocks or corridors generated most complaints? Is there a resource allocation pattern?

themes_detail.label: Vacant Vehicle Accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints totaled 1,651 over the last 90 days (top 5 complaint type by volume), reflecting a chronic infrastructure and public space issue exacerbated by NYPD towing delays—long-running but persistent indicator of neighborhood blight.
evidence: 1,651 abandoned vehicle complaints over 90 days—5th highest complaint category (after illegal parking, heat/hot water, blocked driveway, noise)
Chronic issue not showing acute spike THIS WEEK, but sustained volume indicates systemic problem
Aligns with CB budget priorities around street condition and public space improvement
reporting_angles: Deep dive: what is the average tow wait time for abandoned vehicles reported in East New York vs. citywide average? Why the lag?
Visual investigation: photograph clusters of abandoned vehicles on major streets; interview residents on impact to parking, safety, quality of life.
